title: "Introduction to R for Public Health Surveillance"
date: 2025-10-27
description: "Introduces R for reproducible data handling, analysis, and visualization."
---


### Introduction

R and RStudio are powerful, open-source tools widely used for modern public health data analysis, enabling analysts to manage, explore, visualize, and communicate data-driven insights effectively. 
This module introduces participants to the `R` programming environment and the RStudio interface, with a focus on practical applications in public health surveillance and epidemiological analysis.

Using the `tidyverse` workflow, participants will learn essential data analysis processes, including importing, cleaning, transforming, summarizing, and visualizing health data. 
The module provides hands-on experience with key `R` packages such as `readr`, `dplyr`, `tidyr`, and `ggplot2` for efficient and reproducible analytical workflows.

By the end of the module, participants will be able to apply `R` to perform descriptive analyses, generate meaningful visualizations, interpret disease patterns and trends, and create reproducible reports that support evidence-based public health decision-making.

::: {.callout-tip title="Module Focus"}
Develop practical R skills for managing surveillance datasets, calculating key public health indicators, creating informative visualizations, and producing reproducible analytical outputs for routine public health analysis.
:::

### Prerequisites

Before attending, please ensure you have:

- Completed Workshop 01
- Installed the `sf` package in R: `install.packages("sf")`
- Reviewed the field safety guidelines (see Materials below)
- Brought sturdy footwear and waterproof field sheets
